newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Gandalf seeks creditor protection.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Gandalf seeks creditor protection.

text.p: (All figures in U.S. dollars unless otherwise stated)
In a long-awaited move, beleaguered Canadian computer equipment maker Gandalf Technologies Inc. filed for creditor protection on Friday to allow it to restructure and perhaps find a buyer.
The money-losing firm, based outside Ottawa, added that it cut its North American staff close to 40 percent, laying off 180 employees.

"This restructuring is intended to enable continued operations on a more economically viable basis to allow the opportunity for the company to continue seeking an investor or a partner to acquire all or part of Gandalf," it said in a statement.
Gandalf has struggled since early 1996 when it overhauled its sales distribution system. The move to sell to resellers instead of end-users cost it much of its experienced sales force.
The company lost 43 cents a share in the fourth quarter ended March 31, vs. a break-even year- earlier period.
Gandalf said on June 30 it might need to seek bankruptcy protection after failing to find a buyer or investor earlier this year.

Shares in Gandalf were down 2 cents Canadian to 98 cents Canadian on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Friday, before being halted for news of the bankruptcy filing. Trading did not resume by the close. Gandalf was halted on Nasdaq at 75 cents.
Brian Piccioni, an analyst at Marleau, Lemire Securities, said that a buyer could be interested if the stock tumbled to the 50 cents Canadian (36.5 cent) range.
At that level, Gandalf would be worth about C$20 million ($14.5 million) and up to C$40 million ($29 million) including debt, Piccioni estimated.
But another analyst said that a rescuer would have appeared long ago if there was interest in the company.
